explanation: Fires on a space-prefixed dollar token that follows a prose word and opens a value (' $', ' $\', ' $$\', ' ${\'): strongest (0.6-1.0 of max) when the preceding text is mathematical or quantitative ('for all [$]u$', 'root at about [$]x', 'value of [$]\alpha', 'expected to reach [$]1.4 billion'), and about 0.3-0.5 in casual or code text ('I paid [$]5', Perl 'variable [$]name'), because it cannot see what follows the '$'. A secondary, graded response is on numerals stating an amount after an approximating or quantity word ('around [378]', 'over 200,[000]', 'employs 5,[000]') at 0.3-1.0. Weak activity (0.2-0.4) is on 'all', 'per', '£', '\(' and '\frac' in math-like text. It is near zero on a '$' with no leading space (line-initial '$x$', closing '$'), on jQuery '$("#', on page/chapter/version labels, and on the same prose with the math written without dollars or in parentheses.
